WEB Aruba N.V. ("Customer") is evaluating the integration of two future wind projects, WP-Rincon and WP-Vader Piet II (repowering), with an estimated combined installed capacity of approximately 90 MW. The integration requires a new 60 kV Balance of Plant (BOP) infrastructure to connect these parks to WEB Aruba’s existing Substations EAST and WEST.

Based on the Terms of Reference (TOR) and the subsequent alignment meeting, DNV Netherlands B.V. ("DNV") understands that WEB Aruba will be responsible for the 15 km, 60 kV feeder cables and the main 60/?? kV step-down transformers at the new Rincon substation. WEB Aruba requires a rapid turnaround (2 to 3 months) for a technical feasibility assessment and pre-engineering scope to facilitate an upcoming EPC tendering process.
DNV is pleased to present this proposal to support WEB Aruba with our extensive global expertise in power system integration, substation engineering, and cable routing.

To meet WEB Aruba’s accelerated 2-to-3-month project schedule for the upcoming EPC tender, DNV proposes a targeted, fast-track engineering assessment. Our approach focuses on delivering actionable pre-engineering specifications while mitigating the highest-risk integration elements.
Based on our alignment meeting, DNV’s approach will include:

Rather than performing a full dynamic system impact study from scratch, DNV will conduct targeted analytical studies—specifically short-circuit analysis, steady-state load flow, and frequency scan/resonance checks. This ensures the safe specification of the 60 kV equipment, validates the 100% redundancy sizing of the 15 km cables (~90 MW per feeder), and assesses potential switching overvoltages or capacitive charging issues.

For the ~15 km cable trajectory, DNV will evaluate the ~10 km section running parallel to existing WEB feeders to assess trench capacity and thermal derating. For the new ~5 km section, DNV will leverage existing environmental and routing data previously gathered during the natural gas pipeline trajectory assessment, saving valuable time and reducing permitting uncertainties.

DNV will define the integration requirements for the existing GIS breaker at Substation EAST and the new GIS breaker at Substation WEST. Concurrently, our transformer experts will validate the sizing, impedance, and tap-changer requirements for the two 100%-rated 60/?? kV main step-down transformers at the new Rincon substation.

To deliver the proposed solution, DNV has structured the Scope of Work into five key sequential tasks:
Task 1: Project Initiation, Data Gathering & Basis of Design (BoD)
Conduct a project kick-off meeting with WEB Aruba to finalise communication protocols, project timelines, and confirm the exact Point of Common Coupling (POCC) boundaries.

Review all existing documentation provided by WEB Aruba, including 60 kV network SLDs, GIS switchgear OEM manuals (Substations EAST & WEST), as-built trench data for the ~10 km existing cable route, and any preliminary data from the wind developer.
Develop a concise BoD document defining the electrical parameters, N-1 redundancy criteria, environmental conditions, and design standards that will govern the pre-engineering phase.

Perform analytical calculations to evaluate the integration of ~90 MW into the 60 kV system. This will validate bulk power transfer capabilities, confirm voltage profiles, and assess the fault level impact on the existing 60 kV GIS switchgear.

Given the significant capacitance of dual 15 km, 60 kV underground cables and the large inductance of the ~90 MVA transformers, DNV will perform a frequency scan to identify potential harmonic resonance issues, capacitive charging current limits, and switching overvoltage risks during energisation.
Task 3: Cable System Sizing & Routing Assessment

Perform preliminary continuous current rating and short-circuit sizing calculations per IEC 60287. Cables will be sized to carry 100% of the combined ~90 MW wind capacity to meet N-1 redundancy requirements.
3.2 Thermal Bottleneck Analysis (~10 km existing route):
Evaluate the thermal interaction risks and potential derating for the ~10 km section where the new cables will run parallel to existing WEB feeders.
3.3 Desktop Route Assessment (~5 km new route):

Execute a desktop-based route assessment for the new trajectory leading to the Rincon substation, leveraging historical environmental and routing data from the previously proposed natural gas pipeline project to accelerate the assessment and identify major obstacles or trenching constraints.

Develop preliminary technical specifications for the two 60/?? kV main step-down transformers at the Rincon substation, including validating 100% capacity rating (~90 MVA each), defining impedance, vector group, cooling (ONAN/ONAF), grounding, and evaluating the necessity of an OLTC versus the requested NLTC.
Evaluate the technical capability, control interfaces, and any required modifications to terminate Feeder 1 into the existing 60 kV GIS breaker (STG#3).
Define the technical specifications, physical space requirements, and interlocking/protection logic for integrating a completely new 60 kV GIS breaker bay for Feeder 2.
Task 5: Risk Assessment, CAPEX Estimation & Pre-Engineering Scope

Develop a comprehensive Risk Register identifying technical, constructability, operational, and environmental/permitting risks associated with the BOP infrastructure, with proposed mitigation measures for each identified risk.
Develop an indicative Class 4/5 budgetary estimate (AACE International standard: approx. -30% to +50% accuracy) covering the anticipated equipment, cable supply, and installation costs.

Compile the findings from Tasks 1–4 into a clearly structured, functional Pre-Engineering Scope document, accompanied by a Preliminary Single-Line Diagram (SLD), formatted specifically for WEB Aruba’s EPC tendering process.

In addition to possible assumptions, conditions and limitation stated elsewhere, this proposal is issued on the basis of the following assumptions, conditions and limitation with respect to deliverables, scope of work, schedule and costs etc.:
WEB Aruba will provide existing and up-to-date power system data (single-line diagrams, switchgear OEM manuals, and base load-flow / short-circuit case files) within Week 1 of project commencement.

Full dynamic stability, transient stability, and Grid Code compliance studies are explicitly excluded from the current scope. This proposal is limited to steady-state load flow, short-circuit analysis, and frequency scan / resonance checks only.

The wind developer will confirm the wind farm collector bus voltage level (currently indicated as “?? kV”) no later than Week 2. If not confirmed by that date, DNV will proceed with a 34.5 kV assumption; any subsequent revision will be treated as a scope change.

Substation WEST is assumed to have adequate physical space inside the existing substation perimeter for a new 60 kV GIS breaker bay. Major structural extensions or new building construction are outside this scope.

The desktop cable route assessment for the new ~5 km section will rely on historical natural gas pipeline corridor data. No geotechnical investigations, GPR surveys, or soil thermal resistivity tests are included in this phase.
